# `evidence/` — do these records have a runtime consumer?

**Short answer: no code reads them back to make a decision. One guard scans their raw text.**
Verified 2026-08-23 (H7-deadweight lane), against the files themselves and every tracked
reference to this directory.

## What's here

- `release/acceptance-simulations.json` — regenerated by every `npm run simulate` run
  (`tools/visual-engine/tests/run_simulations.mjs`). Its own `_readme` field says so plainly:
  *"Release acceptance record, regenerated by every `npm run simulate` run. No code reads this
  file back."*
- `validation/*.json` (SIM-01 … SIM-20 etc.) — the tracked golden snapshots `npm run simulate`
  is the **one flow allowed to update** (`adapters/echarts/render.mjs`, comment tagged `P8-066`).
  Every one of these files carries the same self-declaration in its own `_readme` field, e.g.
  `validation/SIM-20-print.json`: *"Documentation/audit trail only — no code in this engine
  reads this file back."*
- `research/RESEARCH_2026-08-08.md` — a dated research note, prose only.

## What was actually verified this pass, not just quoted

1. **Nothing diffs a fresh render against these files.** `grep -rn "evidence/validation" tools/
   visual-engine/tests/*.mjs` returns only the one comment in `run_simulations.mjs` that
   describes writing them — no test reads one back for comparison. A regression in the renderer
   would not be caught by these files; `tools/visual-engine/tests/*.test.mjs`'s own assertions
   are the actual regression gate.
2. **One guard does read them, as text, not as a baseline.**
   `tools/corpus_check/guards/built_claims.py` — the "a documented command must actually be
   runnable" guard — scans every tracked `*.json` file (among other extensions) for embedded
   `npm run <script>` / `python3 -m tools.<pkg>` strings and cross-checks them against real
   `package.json` scripts and real argparse subcommands. That scan covers this whole directory.
   It is why `release/acceptance-simulations.json` needed an explicit exemption
   (`_THIRD_PARTY_RECORDS` in that guard) the day its own `"run": "npm run simulate"` field was
   checked against the wrong package's scripts — the guard's own comment names this file by path.
   The `validation/*.json` files are scanned the same way; none currently embeds a command-like
   string, so none has ever tripped the check, but they are not invisible to it.
3. **`tools/tests/test_corpus_check.py` exercises the above** — it is the only test file (besides
   the guard itself) that names this directory.

## The honest summary

These are write-only audit records for a human or a future debugging session, not inputs to any
gate's pass/fail decision — with the one caveat that their raw text is inside the surface a
completeness guard (`built_claims.py`) scans for stale documented commands. That is a narrower
claim than "has a runtime consumer" and a stronger one than "nobody has ever looked at this
directory" — both of which would be wrong to write here.
